name: FTSE 100
summary: FTSE 100 within 2% of its high, supported by energy and mining shares
state: The FTSE 100 last closed on 30 Oct at 10,730, about 1.7% below its 52-week high. Its heavy weighting to oil, gas and mining companies has cushioned it from the energy shock. London markets reopen on 2 Nov, ahead of the Bank of England decision on 5 Nov.
for_you: The index's resilience reflects its global, commodity-heavy make-up rather than the domestic UK economy, which faces higher energy bills and rising rates.
rubric_hit: Drawdown from 52-week high < 5% and no single-day fall > 2.5% this week.
why: The UK's main index — a gauge of UK-listed multinationals, pensions and sterling-area sentiment.
drivers: Commodity prices, sterling, global risk appetite, UK policy and banking sector news.
